summary: Somerset County, ME wood fire tower on Sally Mountain near Attean, built 1908 and removed in the 1930s; only metal pieces remain near the trail.

facts.status_note: Removed sometime in the 1930s; a trail guide says four pieces of metal remain bolted into the rock near the old tower site

staffing.status: watchman's cabin built in 1908 and photographed in 1932; no watchman named in the sources read

access.note: Reached by a hiking trail; the Forest Society of Maine protects the land; no closure found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Trail guide gives about 3 miles to the summit; the old tower site lies along the final 0.4-mile stretch of trail to the summit. There is no tower to climb.

events.note: Wood tower built as a response to a fire on the mountain (Maine Memory caption); Maine Atlas also gives 1908
Watchman's cabin built the same year
Maine Forest Service panoramic map centered on the tower is dated 1919
Removed sometime in the 1930s (Maine Atlas); the year given is the start of the decade, not a known date
Tower and watchman's cabin photographed in 1932 (Maine Memory); a caption suggests the cabin photo dates from about when the tower came down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1919 map record gives Attean Twp in Sagadahoc County. The Maine Memory record places T5 R1 NBKP in Somerset County, and the Forest Fire Lookout list does the same; the story follows Somerset.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1908 agrees across the Maine Atlas and Maine Memory. Removal is only sometime in the 1930s, so the 1930 event year is a decade placeholder. Summit height differs between sources (Maine Atlas 2221 ft, Maine by Foot 2,227 ft), so no height_m was recorded. The 1908 builder is not named, so no agency is recorded. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook photo caption seen only in a search snippet mentions a watchman in the early 1930s; not used. Maine Memory images are watermarked, educational-use only, so no photo was added.
